answer: Auction rate securities (ARS) are debt or preferred equity securities whose interest rates are reset periodically through auctions—often every 7, 14, 28, or 35 days. Although they were sometimes marketed as cash-equivalent investments, they did not have the same level of liquidity as money market mutual funds or certificates of deposit. If an auction attracted too few bidders to set a clearing rate, investors could face a high or penalty interest rate and might be unable to sell their ARS until a later auction succeeded.
